dataset: Lombard 2021 USGS arsenic, ACR granularity sensitivity
reading: Categorical-baseline ACR is essentially GRANULARITY-INVARIANT: Level-III (fine, 13 regions) ACR 45.5% vs Level-II (coarse, 8 regions) ACR 46.1% (<1-pt difference). This REFUTES the naive hypothesis that finer regions raise ACR. Arsenic's lower ACR vs nitrate/fluoride distance-IDW (~80%) is therefore intrinsic to the baseline FORM, not partition resolution: a categorical region-mean discards within-region distance decay that a continuous IDW kernel retains, so refining/coarsening the partition cannot recover it. The caveat becomes a result: arsenic's ~45% is a valid categorical-form value (the floor a coordinate-free dataset can achieve), not an underestimate.
